claim: All modern humans are descended from a common ancestral population that lived in Africa approximately 200000 to 300000 years ago
Language is a uniquely human capacity that emerged at least 50000 years ago enabling complex social organization and cultural transmission
Cultural relativism holds that cultures should be understood on their own terms rather than judged by the standards of another culture
Gift economies based on reciprocal exchange of goods and services exist in many societies as alternatives to market-based economics
Oral traditions have preserved knowledge histories and cultural values across generations in societies without writing systems
The Sapiens cognitive revolution approximately 70000 years ago enabled humans to cooperate in large groups through shared myths and narratives
Indigenous peoples manage approximately 80 percent of the world remaining biodiversity through traditional ecological knowledge
Music is a cultural universal found in every known human society and appears to predate language in human evolution
The concept of human rights as universal and inalienable emerged from multiple cultural traditions not exclusively from Western Enlightenment thought
Archaeological evidence shows that humans have engaged in long-distance trade networks for at least 300000 years
